ConfirmationArchitecture.description: ORE Section 3.3. Records each confirmation mode present rather than forcing one cell. Party count is not a substitute for independence; where effective independence cannot be assessed, that is recorded as a named flag.

basis.description: The basis for the confirmation-architecture reading.

independence_flag.description: ORE Section 3.3 party-count limit. Set where effective independence cannot be assessed; party count is never a substitute.

modes.description: One or more confirmation modes present when the source produced its output.

ConfirmationArchitecture.title: ConfirmationArchitecture

ConfirmationMode.description: ORE Section 3.3. The confirmation modes a source's output can carry; more than one may be present.
ConfirmationMode.title: ConfirmationMode

ConformanceAnswer.description: ORE Section 8. Per-obligation answer; silence is not one of the values.
ConformanceAnswer.title: ConformanceAnswer

DimensionExposure.description: ORE Section 5. Per-dimension exposure on an output.

weakest_assessment.description: The weakest assessment present anywhere in the support for this dimension.

DimensionExposure.title: DimensionExposure

ExtensionDimension.description: ORE Section 3.4 and Section 7. A declared extension dimension is either graded (with a basis) or its absence is declared with a named reason. The "if not graded then a reason is required" obligation is modeled as a presence-based rule and enforced by a standard JSON Schema validator, so an extension can never fall silent or default to a middle value.

graded.description: The grading of this extension, where the system grades it.

not_applicable_reason.description: ORE Section 7. Where the extension is not graded, the named reason (a genesis limitation for a new source, a permanent property of the source class, or a declared choice not to grade).

resolves_with_history.description: ORE Section 7.3. Whether the limitation is expected to resolve as history accumulates.

ExtensionDimension.title: ExtensionDimension

GradeProfile.description: ORE Section 5. The grade profile an output exposes: for each grading dimension, the weakest assessment present anywhere in the output's support and every flag any source in that support carries. Never a combined figure. This is the companion object to GradedSource, carried on outputs rather than on sources.

joint_support_flag.description: ORE Section 5. Separately admitted sources in the support that cannot be shown distinct in effective origin.

rests_on_open_posture_material.description: ORE Section 5. True where the output rests partly on ungraded material admitted under an Open posture, declared on the face.

GradeProfile.title: GradeProfile

GradedDimension.description: ORE Section 3. A dimension records an assessment and the basis on which it was made. Any sub-assessment that could not be computed is a named flag, never a silent default or an assumed middle value.

assessment.description: The uncertainty assessment on this dimension. Not a quality rank.

basis.description: The basis on which the assessment was made.

flag.description: A named limitation where a sub-assessment could not be computed. Never a silent default.

GradedDimension.title: GradedDimension

GradedSource.description: ORE Section 8. An admitted source carrying its grading: the per-dimension grade, the intake posture in force when it was admitted, any monitoring obligation, and the conformance declaration. This is the unit ORE conformance is assessed against.

conformance.description: ORE Section 8. The four conformance questions answered on the face.

grade.description: ORE Section 3. The per-dimension uncertainty grade of the source.

monitoring.description: ORE Section 4. The monitoring obligation attached to an admitted opaque or flagged source.

posture.description: ORE Section 6.4. The intake posture in force when this source was admitted, recorded so its grading history is never ambiguous later.

standing_loss.description: ORE Section 6. The documented, evidence-based record where this source's eligibility was reduced or withdrawn.

GradedSource.title: GradedSource

IntakePosture.description: ORE Section 6. The intake posture: when grading happens and what ungraded material may touch.
IntakePosture.title: IntakePosture

OreConformance.description: ORE Section 8. The four conformance questions answered on the face. There is deliberately no overall or total field: conformance is per-obligation, mirroring the refusal to combine grades (Section 2) and the Verification-Summary-Attestation shape.
OreConformance.title: OreConformance

OreGrade.description: ORE Section 3. The per-dimension grade. Three dimensions are required (provenance integrity, epistemic soundness, confirmation architecture); two are declared extensions (track record, independence) that must each be addressed, graded or with a declared absence. There is deliberately no combined figure: the closed schema forbids one, which enforces the Section 2 refusal to merge into a single confidence number by absence.

confirmation_architecture.description: ORE Section 3.3. What confirmed the source's output when it was produced.

epistemic_soundness.description: ORE Section 3.2. Is the output structured so independent truth-evaluation is possible.

independence.description: ORE Section 3.4. Declared extension. Graded, or absence declared (Section 7 genesis limitation).

provenance_integrity.description: ORE Section 3.1. Did the input come from where it claims, and arrive unchanged.

track_record.description: ORE Section 3.4. Declared extension. Graded, or absence declared (Section 7 genesis limitation).

OreGrade.title: OreGrade

StandingLoss.description: ORE Section 6. Standing loss is only through a documented, evidence-based process: the evidence, the basis, and the decision are recorded and retained with the source. Adverse findings are never silently discarded. Loss of standing is not retroactive.

evidence.description: The evidence on which standing was reduced or withdrawn.

StandingLoss.title: StandingLoss

description: ORE Section 8. An admitted source carrying its grading: the per-dimension grade, the intake posture in force when it was admitted, any monitoring obligation, and the conformance declaration. This is the unit ORE conformance is assessed against.

conformance.description: ORE Section 8. The four conformance questions answered on the face.

grade.description: ORE Section 3. The per-dimension uncertainty grade of the source.

monitoring.description: ORE Section 4. The monitoring obligation attached to an admitted opaque or flagged source.

posture.description: ORE Section 6.4. The intake posture in force when this source was admitted, recorded so its grading history is never ambiguous later.

standing_loss.description: ORE Section 6. The documented, evidence-based record where this source's eligibility was reduced or withdrawn.
